name: Algolaser Alpha MK2 40W
tagline: 40W Premium open-frame diode focused on speed and fine engraving detail
tldr: Algolaser Alpha MK2 40W is the 40W SKU on the Algolaser algolaser alpha mk2 line. Algolaser targets makers who want faster engraving and tighter spot control than typical budget diodes. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Maximum cut speed and depth in the line: engraving remains strong at tuned speeds

priceRange.note: 40W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Algolaser's settings keep basswood plywood single-pass up to 15 mm (150 mm/min), with 8 mm at 350 mm/min
Highest engraving preset of the line: 30,000 mm/min on basswood plywood
Black acrylic up to 8 mm in one pass at 200 mm/min, twice the 20W's speed
cons: About $420 more than the 20W machine-only ($999 vs $579 in October 2026)
Widest spot of the line at full power (0.175 × 0.15 mm), and a slightly smaller work area (400 × 386 mm)
More smoke at full power: plan an exhaust or the smart enclosure bundle ($1,298)
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 40W SKU on Algolaser Alpha MK2. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Treat engraving and cutting as separate profiles. Push cut speeds only after test squares on your material. Compare CO₂ only when clear acrylic or all-day production enters the picture.

editorialDepth.advantages: Algolaser Alpha MK2 40W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: What thickness does the Alpha MK2 40W handle in a single pass?
faq.answer: Algolaser's settings list basswood plywood in one pass at 1,200 mm/min (2 mm), 750 (3 mm), 700 (4–5 mm), 400 (6 mm), 350 (8 mm), 300 (10 mm), 250 (12–13 mm) and 150 mm/min (14–15 mm). Black acrylic: 3.5 mm at 500 mm/min, 5 mm at 250 and 8 mm at 200, all in one pass; 10 mm needs 4 passes.

faq.question: Does the 40W lose engraving detail?
faq.answer: Slightly at full power: Algolaser specifies 0.175 × 0.15 mm for the 40W against 0.16 × 0.14 mm for the 20W. For photos you will run lower power, and our 10 × 10 cm photo test still finishes in ~6–9 min, the fastest of the line. For portrait work at very fine scale, the 10W's smaller spot keeps an edge.

faq.question: Is the 40W worth it over the 20W?
faq.answer: If you cut 8 mm and thicker stock daily, yes: 8 mm runs at 350 vs 200 mm/min, and 13–15 mm plywood stays single-pass where the 20W needs two. Otherwise the $420 gap (machine-only, October 2026) buys little for engraving-led work. The 40W smart enclosed bundle was $1,298.
